newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges settlement of American Airlines row.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges settlement of American Airlines row.

text.p: President Clinton Friday urged American Airlines and its pilots' union to keep trying to reach a labour contract as a midnight deadline for a strike that would ground the airline fast approached.
"They need to go back to work. They have a few more hours of work to do," Clinton said, looking at his watch, after a reporter asked if he would intervene to avert a strike.
Clinton said he would meet with his advisers later in the day to get an update on the situation.
Deputy White House counsel Bruce Lindsey, one of the president's closest aides, was in constant contact with the parties, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

Under the Railway Labour Act, which also applies to U.S. airlines, Clinton could act to postpone a strike for 60 days. But he and his advisers clearly hoped that American and its pilots would agree on a new contract before the midnight Friday (0500 Saturday GMT) strike deadline set by the union.
